title: Kingdom of Etruria
capsule: The Kingdom of Etruria (Regno di Etruria) was a French client state created by the Treaty of Aranjuez (21 March 1801), carved from the former Grand Duchy of Tuscany and awarded to the Bourbon-Parma dynasty as compensation for Parma's annexation by France. Its first king, Louis I of Etruria, reigned only until 1803 and was succeeded by the infant Louis II under the regency of his mother, Queen María Luisa of Spain. The kingdom fielded a token army of 4,000 men and exercised little independent policy; Napoleon dissolved it in December 1807, dividing the territory into three French imperial departments (Arno, Méditerranée, and Ombrone). After 1815 Tuscany reverted to the Austrian Habsburgs and the Duchy of Lucca was created as Bourbon compensation.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's boundaries are well documented through the Treaty of Aranjuez and French administrative records; they correspond closely to the pre-existing Grand Duchy of Tuscany.
